Subject: Questions on credits, stacking and Dedicated eligibility for our cohort

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Nebula Studio runs a seasonal accelerator and we’re trying to clarify how Redwood’s promotional credits and startup discounts can be applied across our cohort. A few things procurement flagged:

- Can promo / onboarding credits be pooled centrally and used to pay for Dedicated or Reserved capacity, or are they strictly for Hosted API consumption?
- If credits are pooled, can they be allocated to specific teams after the cohort (i.e., transferability / partial redemptions)?
- Does the 30% startup discount stack with promotional credits, or is it mutually exclusive? Procurement prefers clear invoiceable items and an option that lets us move to Dedicated capacity mid-pilot.

I’ve attached a small cohort participant CSV for sizing. Procurement will need a proforma if we move forward. Timeline: we need a procurement-ready path by next Tuesday, ideally.

Best,

Sofia / Laura —

I put together three options that balance procurement simplicity and flexibility. See short summary below; I’ve attached a spreadsheet with per-seat math.

Option A — Hosted-first (simple, fastest)
- Promotional/onboarding credits applied only to Hosted usage.
- Startup discount (30%) applies to Hosted invoice line items; credits consumed before discount.
- No transfer to Dedicated.
- Good when cohort usage remains bursty and you want minimal billing ops.

Option B — Dedicated-premise reservation (predictable)
- Offer a small Dedicated pool (min 2 GPU-equivalent units) with a 15% discount.
- Promotional credits used as a one-time offset to the first month invoice only.
- Requires a 3-month minimum commit.

Option C — Hybrid bridge + convert (recommended for Nebula)
- Pool promotional credits to cover initial Hosted consumption across cohort.
- Nebula can elect a conversion window (within first 90 days) to convert remaining credits into a Dedicated prepay at a conversion rate (e.g., 1 credit unit -> $0.62 toward Dedicated commit).
- If converted, apply an additional cohort loyalty discount (10%) to the Dedicated rate for the first 6 months.
- Finance creates a proforma showing credits applied then a conversion invoice if exercised.

Risks / notes:
- Finance will need final language on credit expirations and transferability.
- Legal may want credit usage limited to the account and cohort participants (no open marketplace transfers).

Next step: if Nebula likes Option C, I can prepare a proforma (PDF) + a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones: PO, proforma sign, trial start, conversion decision.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — Nebula procurement ran the numbers and prefers Option C (hybrid bridge + convert). A couple of clarifying asks before we get the PO:

1) Conversion rate: can Redwood make the conversion rate fixed in the proforma (we need line-item clarity for our accounting team)?
2) Rollover: if any promo credits remain after 90 days and Nebula doesn’t convert, what happens? Do they expire or roll to next cohort?

Procurement is also asking about tax treatment for the converted prepay. If you can flag that for finance on the proforma that would help. We can target a PO by Tuesday EOD if the proforma is clean.

—Ethan

Ben / Laura — quick confirmation before I send the proforma to Nebula:

- We will lock the conversion rate in the proforma (example: 1 credit unit = $0.62 toward Dedicated commit) and include a clause that it is valid for 7 calendar days from issuance.
- Unconverted promo credits expire after 90 days and do not auto-roll to future cohorts (we can offer an exception in writing for enterprise customers but not as standard).
- Finance will add a tax note; proforma will be explicit about the taxable amount for the converted prepay.
- Include MAP link and HubSpot deal id on the proforma.

If that all looks good I’ll attach the proforma and MAP link to the email to Ava/Ethan.
